articles.headline: Tottenham's winning run brought to abrupt end by late Noah Okafor winner
articles.description: Noah Okafor stepped off the bench to snatch Leeds three points as they beat Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road to snap their five-game winless Premier League run.
articles.headlineJa: トッテナムの快進撃に終止符、終盤のノア・オカフォーによる決勝ゴール
articles.descriptionJa: リーズ・ユナイテッドがエランド・ロードでトッテナムを1-0で下し、プレミアリーグ5試合連続無勝利の記録を脱した。途中出場したノア・オカフォーが決勝ゴールを決め、リーズに勝ち点3をもたらした。
articles.body:
Noah Okafor stepped off the bench to snatch Leeds three points as they beat Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road to snap their five-game winless Premier League run.

Okafor struck with his first touch, two minutes after replacing Lukas Nmecha, to seal Leeds' third league win of the season and condemn resurgent Tottenham to their first defeat in five.

The Londoners were chasing their fourth straight win having shot up the table from bottom to ninth place before kick-off, but in a game of few clear-cut chances Okafor's introduction proved decisive.

James Trafford gifted Bournemouth their opening goal last week with a misplaced pass, but he appeared to have put that behind him, cleanly catching an early cross and then picking out his man with a low clearance.

Trafford spoke this week of his "horrendous" spell at Manchester City last season, saying he had to leave for the sake of his mental wellbeing after playing second fiddle to Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But he is thriving in his number one role at Elland Road and after Ao Tanaka and Ethan Ampadu had fired off target, the England goalkeeper showed his confidence remains undiminished.

He punched clear a dangerous cross from Mohammed Kudus and, as Tottenham began to find their stride, saved well down to his right from Omar Marmoush's low shot.

Home fans appealed for a penalty when a cross appeared to hit Mateus Fernandes on the arm, but VAR ruled otherwise.

Leeds were wasteful with their balls into the box and they breathed a huge sigh of relief deep in the first half when a lengthy VAR check concluded no serious foul play after Jayden Bogle's studs had accidentally caught Mathys Tel on his Achilles.

After Nmecha, who made his first start of the season, had headed straight at Tottenham goalkeeper Antonín Kinsky, Tel was unable to continue and was replaced by Dominic Solanke.

Leeds stepped it up after the restart. Dominic Calvert-Lewin's header was blocked, Nico Elvedi nodded his follow-up wide and Tanaka fired over the crossbar.

A spell of concerted pressure from the home side raised the noise levels, with Nmecha crowded out after being played into the box.

Tottenham substitute Conor Gallagher flashed a 20-yard shot inches wide and, with the game on a knife's edge, Ampadu lashed over after Bogle's initial effort had been blocked.

Kinsky then produced the save of the match to tip Sean Longstaff's volley over the crossbar - the former Newcastle midfielder made his first league start in almost a year - as Leeds chased the winner.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke sent on Harry Wilson and Okafor for Tanaka and Nmecha with 13 minutes left and it proved a masterstroke as his side broke the deadlock two minutes later.

Wilson played in Okafor with his first touch following a long throw into the box and the Switzerland striker ran on to rifle his finish beyond Kinsky for his second league goal of the season.

articles.headline: Diego Simeone backs Julián Álvarez for Barcelona clash after Atlético transfer saga
articles.description: Diego Simeone has said Julián Álvarez is ready to take on Barcelona in this weekend's top of the table clash after failing to secure a move in the summer.
articles.headlineJa: ディエゴ・シメオネ、移籍騒動を経てフリアン・アルバレスにバルセロナ戦への期待を寄せる
articles.descriptionJa: 夏の移籍が実現しなかったフリアン・アルバレスについて、ディエゴ・シメオネは今週末の首位同士の直接対決となるバルセロナ戦に向けて、準備はできていると語った。
articles.body:
Diego Simeone has said Julián Álvarez is ready to take on Barcelona in Sunday's top-of-the-table clash in LaLiga (watch live on ESPN+ at 3 p.m. ET) after failing to secure a move to the Spanish champions in the summer.

Álvarez, 26, told ESPN in June that he wanted to leave Atlético Madrid, with sources confirming his preference was to join Barça.

However, Atlético refused to transfer Álvarez to their title rivals, ignoring a €100 million ($111.5m) offer, and the Argentina forward ended up staying at the Metropolitano.

He will face Barça for the first time since the saga drew to a close this weekend when LaLiga's top two, who are separated by just two points, meet in Madrid.

"He's doing very good," was Atlético coach Simeone's limited response in a news conference Saturday when asked if Álvarez was prepared to face Barça.

Álvarez was jeered by Atlético fans earlier in the season for trying to engineer a move away, but he has since apologised for his actions.

The summer's events also meant he featured infrequently at the start of the campaign, but he has now started Atlético's last four matches, scoring twice.

Barça coach Hansi Flick was keen to add Álvarez to his attack following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres and remains a fan of the former Manchester City striker.

"For me, Julián Álvarez is a fantastic player, but he is playing for Atlético," Flick said in a news conference. "I have to focus on my team."

One attacker Barça did sign in the summer was Anthony Gordon, who has become a fixed part of the team's attacking trio alongside Raphinha and Lamine Yamal.

Speaking earlier this week, Gordon, who has scored three goals and provided four assists this season, said Barça supporters have not seen the best of him yet and promised to become more selfish.

Flick has been happy with the England international's start to life in Spain but agreed with his assessment.

"For me, he gives us a lot with the ball," he said. "He keeps the ball. When we are in ball possession, he makes no easy mistakes.

"But in the final third, I think also he could be more selfish, 1 vs. 1 situations, also like that.

"The last games are very good. He increased his level, what he gives to the team. I am happy with this."

- Barça's Rodri (hamstring) out of Atlético clash

Flick confirmed defenders Eric García and Andreas Christensen will both return to the squad for the Atlético game, with a decision to be made on whether García or youngster Brian Fariñas start at right-back.

Elsewhere, either Frenkie de Jong or Marc Bernal will come in for Rodri, who has been ruled out of the match with a hamstring problem.

For Atlético, United States midfielder Johnny Cardoso is available again, but Cuti Romero remains sidelined with an injury.

articles.descriptionJa: 怪我やバイウィーク、厳しい対戦カードによってラインナップの調整が必要な場合は、マット・ボーエンが推奨する選択肢をリストアップしている。
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

Let's start the Week 9 list at the quarterback position with two players who have positive matchups (based on the numbers). After that, we will pivot to the wide receiver spot, and I've gone a little deeper than usual, with five pass catchers who bring stable floors to the lineup. I also have three running backs who can be played as flex in deeper leagues, plus a tight end who has quietly put together three straight weeks of quality production. As always, we'll end with D/ST, but it's pretty lean out there right now.

Quarterbacks

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (26.6% rostered; at Philadelphia Eagles)

McCarthy scored 10.18 points in Week 7, completing 20-of-28 for 252 yards. McCarthy failed to throw a touchdown, and the rushing totals were down (one carry, one yard), but he is seeing the field with speed and driving the ball from the pocket. With a matchup Sunday versus an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom 10 versus quarterbacks, McCarthy has value in superflex formats.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (18.4% rostered; vs. Detroit Lions)

Willis is averaging 19.8 points over his past three games, with multiple touchdown throws in two of them. Plus, he brings a dual-threat element to the lineup as Willis is averaging 32.1 yards rushing this season with a touchdown in two of his past three games. Given Willis' rising numbers, he's a smart play this week versus a Lions defense that has allowed a league-worst 24.8 points per game to opposing quarterbacks.

Wide receivers

Malik Washington, Miami Dolphins (39.4% rostered; vs. Detroit Lions)

Washington scored a season-high 15 points in Week 8 as he caught his first touchdown of the season. He's now posted double-digit points in four of his past five games. With his route/alignment versatility, Washington will also see rushing attempts, and he gets a quality matchup versus a Lions defense that ranks in the bottom five versus wide receivers.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (44.3% rostered; vs. Dallas Cowboys)

I would take the matchup with Allen versus the Dallas defense Sunday. This Cowboys unit ranks in the bottom 10 versus wide receivers and Allen has scored 13 or more points in two of his past three games. The touchdown upside is limited with Allen, but he can still uncover and find space as an outlet. After catching all seven of his targets for 67 yards versus the Jaguars last week, Allen can be played as high-floor WR3.

articles.body:
Welcome to Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Jaguars-Ravens game.

Teams on bye in Week 9: Steelers, Titans

Week 9 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ MIA

It's hard for a RB to average 28 fantasy points per game. Last season's leader averaged 24.5.
 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs ARI

His updated receiving yards pace is 2,093. He is overcoming the team's QB.
 3. Puka Nacua, WR2 @ WSH

As long as he averages 12-plus targets per game, he will thrive.
 4. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 vs NYJ

Underwhelming games the past two weeks, but this week he faces the Jets.
 5. Brock Purdy, QB1 vs LV

Comes off the bye week ready to blast the Raiders' defense.
 6. Joe Burrow, QB2 @ ATL

 7. Drake Maye, QB3 vs GB

 8. CeeDee Lamb, WR3 @ IND

He's not the reason they lose games. Big game coming against the feeble Colts.
 9. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR4 @ MIA

He hasn't scored a TD since Week 3, but perhaps it changes versus the Dolphins this week.
 10. Josh Allen, QB4 @ MIN

The matchup with a stingy Vikings is reason for a lower ranking than typical.
 11. Jared Goff, QB5 @ MIA

 12. Jayden Daniels, QB6 vs LAR

 13. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 vs LV

 14. Bijan Robinson, RB4 vs CIN

 15. Ja'Marr Chase, WR5 @ ATL

Incredible talent just had his first 100-yard receiving game in Week 8.
 16. Tee Higgins, WR6 @ ATL

The QB is so good that yes, the Bengals boast a pair of WR1 options.
 17. Brock Bowers, TE1 @ SF

Yep, we basically view him as a top-five wide receiver now. He's that dominant.
 18. Dak Prescott, QB7 @ IND

His rushing TD versus the Cardinals saved what would have been a disappointing fantasy effort.
 19. Patrick Mahomes, QB8 vs NYJ

Bounced back from the Seahawks debacle with 25.44 fantasy points against the Broncos.
 20. James Cook III, RB5 @ MIN

He has scored a TD in six consecutive games. The Vikings are tough, but you can't sit him.
 21. Jonathan Taylor, RB6 vs DAL

Will he still be a Colt on Sunday? Pay attention to the news. The Colts may sit him.
 22. Justin Jefferson, WR7 vs BUF

 23. Malik Nabers, WR8 @ PHI

 24. Chuba Hubbard, RB7 vs DEN

 25. Javonte Williams, RB8 @ IND

It feels like time for his second 100-yard rushing game of the season.
 26. Kyren Williams, RB9 @ WSH

Only four running backs have more points, but he is sharing more touches now.
 27. Caleb Williams, QB9 vs TB

He averages 19.5 fantasy points. The Buccaneers are defending well, but you can't sit him.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Four players whose upgraded skill sets look real
articles.description: Which players have added new dimensions to their game? Here are four who can sustain their newly-demonstrated skills.
articles.body:
Baseball analyst Ron Shandler famously posited that once a player has demonstrated a skill over a sufficiently meaningful sample, they own it. The key qualifier is that the skill must be demonstrated over a sustained period, not merely in an isolated performance or brief hot streak.

This concept applies to basketball as well. Once a player demonstrates they can effectively protect the rim over multiple months, we can assume they "own" that skill as part of their overall skill set. It was clear early in Walker Kessler's career with the Utah Jazz that he was a special rim protector -- a skill that has proved enduring.

We learn to trust what players can and cannot do on the court over time. Box scores create precedents. Past demonstrated ability deserves more weight than recent struggles because a skill can lie dormant without disappearing.

Which players are establishing new levels of expertise so far this season? Even with the sample size remaining quite small, we can begin to identify new identities around the league. With this lens in mind, let's discuss a quartet of players who have added new dimensions to their real and fantasy reputations thus far.

The prospect who was promised

Incredibly fun and prestigious player comparisons -- to the likes of Rashard Lewis and even Chris Bosh -- surfaced when Jabari Smith Jr. was evaluated during the 2022 NBA draft cycle. While those were lofty comparisons, they spoke to Smith's potential to go beyond a traditional "3-and-D" archetype and develop into a game-changing two-way force.

We're not quite at the All-Star tier for Smith, but it's becoming clear that he is taking ownership of a new level of shooting and scoring. Even though his shot diet this year is identical to last season's, he has leapt nearly 20% in scoring output thanks to appreciable spikes in shooting success. There is danger in simply trusting a hot streak. A more granular look shows Smith is finally thriving off the dribble and as a pull-up shooter, which is also showing up in his ability to initiate and finish drives.

Smith has already proven he owns a unique ability to protect the rim from an atypical position, as his career 2.5% block percentage reveals. The blend of improved shooting and scoring, along with his ability to create turnovers, has Smith positioned 20th overall on the Player Rater, just ahead of Houston Rockets teammate Alperen Sengun. Even when his outside shooting cools -- and it will -- Smith has leveled up enough to remain an impact player.

The ready rookie

Beyond being an amazing soundbite and the oldest prospect in his class, Yaxel Lendeborg was a somewhat mysterious prospect. Dominant rebounding numbers over a long college career did not necessarily indicate a dynamic offensive package.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic's 53-point explosion pushes scoring average past 40 as Lakers roll
articles.description: Luka Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points in a 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers, raising his scoring average to 40.1 PPG.
articles.headlineJa: ルカ・ドンチッチが53得点の猛攻で平均得点40点超え、レイカーズは快進撃を続ける
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜日のブレイザーズ戦で124-118と勝利した試合で、ルカ・ドンチッチがシーズンハイの53得点を記録し、平均得点を40.1点にまで引き上げた。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Though Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and James Harden came somewhat close, no NBA player has averaged at least 40 points in a season since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63.

Believe it or not, Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is on pace through his first nine games of the season to reach that historic benchmark thanks to his latest 50-point explosion.

Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points to lead the Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. The Slovenian star is averaging a career-high 40.1 points and is captaining the NBA's No. 1 offense.

"Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball," Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

Chamberlain is the only player to score more than Doncic's 361 points through his first nine games in a season. The Hall of Fame center had 472 points through nine games in 1962-63 and 455 points in the 1961-62 season, according to ESPN Research.

Chamberlain went on to average an NBA record 50.4 points in 1961-62 and 44.8 points in 1962-63. Jordan's 37.1 points per game in 1986-87 is the NBA's highest mark during the 3-point era. Harden's 36.1 points per game in 2018-19 was the most prolific scoring season of the 21st century. And Bryant's 35.4 points were the most by a Lakers player since the NBA/ABA merger in 1976.

Can Doncic, whose career high for a season is 33.9 points per game with the 2023-24 Dallas Mavericks, join Chamberlain in averaging at least 40 points?

"It's obviously a long season," Doncic said. "We're 10 games in. We've got 72 left. As long as we're winning, I'm good. I got [the shots] up today, I'm not going to lie. Hopefully, it continues, but you never know."

Doncic, 27, is taking full advantage of his new role as the undisputed face of the Lakers after LeBron James' offseason departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. Entering Friday, Doncic was leading the league in scoring, shot attempts, 3-point attempts, free throw attempts, usage rate, player efficiency rating and win shares.

Against the Blazers, Doncic exceeded 40 points for the sixth time this season and topped 50 for the second time. He ranks tied for 10th all time with 11 career games of scoring at least 50 points and is fifth among active players, trailing only Harden, Stephen Curry, Damian Lillard and James.

Doncic, whose 62-foot heave at the halftime buzzer keyed Friday's comeback win, joined Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan as the only Lakers to score at least 40 points in four consecutive games.

"[Doncic] is the MVP right now," Blazers coach Micah Nori said during his pregame comments. "Hands down."

              Portland, Oregon; Saturday, 10 p.m. EST

articles.headline: Atlanta faces Brooklyn, looks for 4th straight victory
articles.description: Brooklyn Nets (2-6, 13th in the Eastern Conference) vs. Atlanta Hawks (6-4, fourth in the Eastern Conference)
articles.headlineJa: アトランタがブルックリンと対戦、4連勝を狙う
articles.descriptionJa: ブルックリン・ネッツ（2勝6敗、東カンファレンス13位）vs アトランタ・ホークス（6勝4敗、東カンファレンス4位）
articles.body:
Brooklyn Nets (2-6, 13th in the Eastern Conference) vs. Atlanta Hawks (6-4, fourth in the Eastern Conference)


              Atlanta; Saturday, 7:30 p.m. EST


              LINE: Hawks -6.5; over/under is 224.5


              BOTTOM LINE: Atlanta will look to keep its three-game win streak going when the Hawks take on Brooklyn.


              Atlanta went 46-36 overall and 27-25 in Eastern Conference play a season ago. The Hawks averaged 118.5 points per game last season, 16.6 on free throws and 43.8 from beyond the arc.


              Brooklyn finished 20-62 overall and 14-37 in Eastern Conference games during the 2025-26 season. The Nets allowed opponents to score 115.9 points per game and shoot 49.7% from the field last season.


              INJURIES: Hawks: Jock Landale: day to day (hip), Henri Veesaar: out for season (acl), Mouhamed Gueye: out (foot), Asa Newell: out (toe), Keshon Gilbert: out (knee), Jalen Johnson: day to day (ankle).


              Nets: Egor Demin: out (leg), Noah Clowney: day to day (knee).

articles.headline: Chicago takes on Philadelphia, aims to halt 6-game slide
articles.description: Philadelphia 76ers (8-2, first in the Eastern Conference) vs. Chicago Bulls (1-7, 14th in the Eastern Conference)
articles.headlineJa: シカゴがフィラデルフィアに挑む、6連敗からの脱出を目指す
articles.descriptionJa: フィラデルフィア・76ers（8勝2敗、東カンファレンス1位）vs シカゴ・ブルズ（1勝7敗、東カンファレンス14位）
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers (8-2, first in the Eastern Conference) vs. Chicago Bulls (1-7, 14th in the Eastern Conference)


              Chicago; Sunday, 3:30 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Chicago heads into the matchup against Philadelphia as losers of six in a row.


              Chicago finished 31-51 overall, 19-32 in Eastern Conference play and 18-23 at home during the 2025-26 season. The Bulls averaged 28.5 assists per game on 42.4 made field goals last season.


              Philadelphia finished 45-37 overall and 27-25 in Eastern Conference play during the 2025-26 season. The 76ers gave up 116.1 points per game while committing 20.3 fouls last season.


              The teams meet for the second time this season. The 76ers won 126-107 in the last matchup on Nov. 3.


              INJURIES: Bulls: Jalen Smith: day to day (hand), Nic Claxton: day to day (hamstring).


              76ers: Ariel Hukporti: out for season (achilles), Adem Bona: day to day (spine), Dominick Barlow: out (back).

articles.headline: Doncic leads Los Angeles against Detroit after 40-point showing
articles.description: Los Angeles Lakers (7-2, first in the Western Conference) vs. Detroit Pistons (6-2, third in the Eastern Conference)
articles.headlineJa: 40得点を記録したドンチッチが、デトロイト戦でロサンゼルスを牽引
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・レイカーズ（7勝2敗、西カンファレンス1位）vs デトロイト・ピストンズ（6勝2敗、東カンファレンス3位）
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers (7-2, first in the Western Conference) vs. Detroit Pistons (6-2, third in the Eastern Conference)


              Detroit; Sunday, 6 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Los Angeles visits the Detroit Pistons after Luka Doncic scored 40 points in the Lakers' 116-103 victory over the Sacramento Kings.


              Detroit finished 60-22 overall with a 32-9 record at home during the 2025-26 season. The Pistons gave up 109.6 points per game while committing 22.0 fouls last season.


              Los Angeles went 53-29 overall with a 25-16 record on the road last season. The Lakers gave up 114.6 points per game while committing 18.5 fouls last season.


              INJURIES: Pistons: Jalen Duren: out (hamstring), Isaiah Joe: day to day (hip).


              Lakers: None listed.
